about: The flat/first serve of a right-hander (Alcaraz), measured at real speed, plus the left-hander's mirror (Shelton). Times are seconds relative to contact (negative = before). Heights and distances are fractions of standing height H (multiply by heightM). Angles in degrees: joint flexion (0 = straight) or segment angle from vertical. Owner: Biomechanics Coach.

measuredFrom.timing: 8 Alcaraz serves in Ryan's US Open clips vs Shelton (Apple Vision 2D pose, ~56 fps, real time, broadcast camera behind his baseline). Players separated from the crowd by datasets/anatomy/tools/uso_tracks.py, measured by measure.py → uso/measurements.json. One serve starts mid-motion (uso-2, frame 0) and one is quicker than the rest (uso-4: maybe a second serve); medians are robust to both.
measuredFrom.angles: The same serves. Seen from behind a side-on server, knee and elbow bends lie close to the picture plane, so they read well; trunk rotation does not show.
measuredFrom.leftHanded: datasets/serves/shelton/compilation-25/26 (4 serves, slow motion: angles only) and 10 other pros in the same compilation for comparison.
measuredFrom.calibration: Lengths use neck→ankle = 0.78 H (Drillis & Contini 1966); expect ±10%.

sources: Kovacs M, Ellenbecker T. An 8-stage model for evaluating the tennis serve. Sports Health 2011;3(6):504–513 (phase names and order).
Elliott B, Fleisig G, Nicholls R, Escamilla R. J Sci Med Sport 2003;6(1):76–87 (max shoulder external rotation ≈ 170°, proximal-to-distal sequence).

events.name: tossArmPassesShoulder
events.what: The toss hand (ball) rises past shoulder height. The weight has already rocked back and forward.

events.name: tossArmHighest
events.what: Toss arm straight up (within 7° of vertical, elbow ~8° bent), hand 1.33 H above the ground: the ball has just left the fingers.

events.name: deepestKnees
events.what: Loading / trophy: knees most bent, toss arm still up, racket hand low behind the back. From here the legs drive up.

events.name: contact
events.what: Racket arm nearly straight and close to vertical, body off the ground.

events.name: landing
events.what: Lands on the front foot inside the court; the back leg kicks up behind for balance.

order: legs (knee + ankle extension, push up and forward)
trunk (uncoils; shoulders tilt: racket shoulder goes from low to high)
shoulder (racket arm external rotation, then fast internal rotation)

timing.note: measured: knee extension starts at the deepest bend; feet leave the ground just before contact
approximate, from the proximal-to-distal sequence (Elliott 2003); not visible from behind
approximate; measured trunk lean grows from 11° (loading) to 18° at contact
racket drop: the racket head points at the ground behind the back (Elliott 2003)
measured: 127° bent at the loading, 13° at contact
pronation and wrist flexion through contact

body.note: side-on: front (left) shoulder points at the net

front.what: straight, front foot at the baseline pointing toward the net post

back.what: bent, weight rocked back onto it

racket.where: in front of the body at waist height, the racket pointing at the target

toss.where: in front, ball against the strings or at the chest

racket.where: hanging at the side, dropping back past the hip

toss.where: in front of the chest, rising straight (nearly horizontal now)

body.note: shoulder-over-shoulder: the racket shoulder is clearly lower than the toss shoulder

legs.note: the knees start bending as the arm goes up

racket.where: still low, at the side/back of the hip (the racket hand starts up only now)

toss.where: straight up, slightly in front of the shoulders

legs.note: the back knee bends more; game captured motions bend 70–90°, the compilation pros 31–58° (front)

racket.where: behind the body (back side of the chest line), elbow bending fast: the racket is going into the drop

toss.where: still pointing up at the ball, above the front shoulder

body.note: off the ground (feet ~0.1–0.15 H up; the game's captured serves: 0.16–0.19 H). Hip height is not given: he moves into the court, so the picture overstates it. Trunk tilted up toward the racket side; racket shoulder now above the toss shoulder

racket.where: straight up, slightly in front of the head and toward the net

toss.where: pulled down and in, tucked against the chest/belly (front of the body); elbow folded but ≤ 145–150°

body.note: chest now faces the net; knees soften to absorb the landing

front.what: lands on it, inside the baseline

back.what: kicked up behind for balance, foot off the ground

racket.where: swung across the body to the non-racket side (left hip for a right-hander), in front

toss.where: out to the side / slightly behind for balance

seenFromBehind.about: Where the arms are on screen for the near player (camera behind), so the sprite puts them on the right side of the torso.
seenFromBehind.rightHanded: Side-on, facing screen-RIGHT. Toss (left) arm: in front of the chest = screen-right of the torso, on the far side of the body (behind the torso until it rises above the head). Racket (right) arm: on the near side (closest to the camera), so it is drawn OVER the torso; at the loading the hand is at the back = screen-left of the spine; at contact it is straight up, a little screen-right of the head; after contact it crosses to screen-right at hip height.
seenFromBehind.leftHanded: Mirror image: facing screen-LEFT, toss (right) arm goes up screen-left in front, racket (left) arm drawn over the torso, loading screen-right of the spine, finishing across to screen-left.

leftHanded.rule: A left-hander's serve is the right-hander's mirrored: swap every left/right joint and flip x. Toss arm = RIGHT, front leg = RIGHT, racket arm = LEFT.
leftHanded.vsRightHanded: Same sequence and the same near-straight contact arm. Shelton loads the front knee a little more (49° vs Alcaraz's 41° in the same compilation) and both knees about evenly; Alcaraz bends the back knee more than the front. Every right-hander in the compilation (Alcaraz, Sinner, Djokovic, Fritz, Medvedev, Rublev, Tsitsipas, de Minaur, Rune) tosses with the left arm.
